answer: Because the timing is logged against the sable challenge, the juniper audit can replay the ocean history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 342 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A scripted farm thus has to pad 181 submissions and hold each account open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
